title: [2611.03049] Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
note: Abstract page, v1 of 2 Nov 2026, eess.SY, the only version; article licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Two-stage method (ARMSL) for feeder active and reactive power: a residual-ordered scenario model, then calibration of the extreme quantiles only, against a simple anchor forecast. Headline: 0.99-quantile pinball loss 0.1932 on FeederBW, 30 to 85% below three baselines. No code link on the page.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Setup. FeederBW: 200 German low-voltage feeders, P and Q averaged to 10 min, direct forecasts at 10, 20, 30 and 60 min; training cutoff 31 Mar 2024, then 42,508 calibration and 567,908 evaluation cases (span in days not stated). Rolle: 24 Swiss meters, 10-min, Jan 2018 to Jan 2019; 28 days calibrate Stage II, the next 53 days evaluate it. All parameters are re-estimated per dataset.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Inputs: observed P, Q, temperature, solar irradiance and calendar features, all as available at issue time (current values, anomalies against month-hour medians, causal filters); no future weather path is fed. Baselines WI-TFT, DiffLoad and OFDDT are said to share issue times, targets, causal inputs and evaluation cases. Neural baselines ran on a GPU; Stage II runs on CPU.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Table I, FeederBW, active-power 0.99 quantile: pinball 0.1932 for ARMSL against 0.2764 (WI-TFT), 0.4225 (DiffLoad), 1.3170 (OFDDT), i.e. 30.08%, 54.27% and 85.33% lower; the gap to WI-TFT has a site-clustered 95% interval of 27.40 to 32.50%. Exceedance 1.054% against a nominal 1% (WI-TFT 6.946%, DiffLoad 0.126%, OFDDT 36.897%).

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Stage I alone: energy and variogram scores 11.02% and 37.46% below DiffLoad, 23.58% and 28.49% below OFDDT. The paper states that WI-TFT scores better than ARMSL on the full distribution; ARMSL's edge over it is at the extreme quantiles. Gains over WI-TFT are 49 to 56% in inferred shock states and between -15.6% and +12.5% outside them.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Rolle: tail-loss reductions against the active-power-only anchor of 5.39, 5.83, 6.29 and 14.40% at 10, 20, 30, 60 min (7.61, 7.25, 8.72, 11.31% on FeederBW); three seeds, 95% intervals with positive lower bounds. The neural baselines are not reported on Rolle. The authors call it a test after local refitting, not a transfer of fixed parameters.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (full text)
note: Event rates from the unchanged Stage I scenarios: correlation 0.953 between predicted and observed feeder rates at the 0.99 threshold, 90.0% of feeders within two points (WI-TFT 86.0%). Stage II has 112 parameters and fits in 2.37 min on CPU; Stage I cost is not measured. The text has no code or weights statement, no repository link and no pre-registration; no model is released.

title: Real-world energy data of 200 feeders from low-voltage grids with metadata in Germany over two years
note: FeederBW data record (Netze BW and KIT), v1.0, open. One-minute measurements for 200 low-voltage feeders, a metadata file, and hourly weather from the DWD ICON-D2 model. Usage notes recommend 1 Apr 2023 to 31 Mar 2024 for training and 1 Apr 2024 to 31 Mar 2025 for testing. Its companion repository (KIT-IAI/FeederBW, not fetched) is described as data loading and small examples, not ARMSL.

title: Hierarchical Demand Forecasting Benchmark for the Distribution Grid
note: Rolle data record, v1 (a newer version exists), open. Power measurements for 24 meters in Rolle, Switzerland, with numerical weather forecasts from a commercial provider refreshed every 12 hours (temperature, irradiance and others, 24-hour paths). So forecast weather exists in this data set, though the ARMSL paper describes its weather inputs as values available at issue time.

title: Hierarchical Demand Forecasting Benchmark for the Distribution Grid
note: Named by the research call, not fetched; from its source entry only. The Rolle benchmark paper: 24 nodes averaging about 81 kW, 10-minute power data from 13 Jan 2018 to 19 Jan 2019, weather forecasts at hourly steps updated every 12 hours. Context for the second data set; not a source for ARMSL's results.

title: Research task (standard): primary sources for or against arXiv 2611.03049
